source_text: Καὶ τοῦτο φανερῶς μὲν οὐκ ἠθέλησεν εἰπεῖν, δι' αἰνιγμάτων δὲ, ὥστε μὴ θορυβῆσαι πάλιν αὐτούς. Ὥσπερ οὖν ὅταν ἀκούσῃς αὐτοῦ λέγοντος, ὅτι Ὃ ἠκούσατε εἰς τὸ οὖς, κηρύξατε ἐπὶ τῶν δωμάτων, καὶ ὃ ἠκούσατε ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ, εἴπατε ἐν τῷ φωτὶ, οὐ τοῦτο ὑποπτεύεις, ὅτι κελεύει τοὺς στενωποὺς καὶ τὴν ἀγορὰν ἀφέντας ἐπὶ τῶν δωμάτων κηρύττειν· οὐδὲ γὰρ φαίνονται τοῦτο ποιήσαντες οἱ μαθηταί· ἀλλὰ τὸ, Ἐπὶ τῶν δωμάτων, καὶ τὸ, Ἐν τῷ φωτὶ, τὸ μετὰ παῤῥησίας αἰνίττεται· τὸ δὲ, Εἰς τὸ οὖς, καὶ τὸ, Ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ, τοῦτο δηλοῖ, ὅτι Ὅπερ ἐν μικρῷ μέρει τῆς οἰκουμένης, καὶ ἐν ἑνὶ χωρίῳ τῆς Παλαιστίνης ἠκούσατε, τοῦτο πανταχοῦ τῆς γῆς ἐξ ηχήσατε. Οὐ γὰρ δὴ ἐν σκοτίᾳ, οὐδὲ εἰς τὸ οὖς διελέγετο αὐτοῖς, ἀλλ' ἐφ' ὑψηλῶν τῶν ὀρέων, καὶ ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς πολλάκις. Οὕτω καὶ ἐνταῦθα ὑποληπτέον. Ὥσπερ οὖν ἐκεῖ δώματα ἀκούοντες, ἑτέρως ἐνοήσαμεν, οὕτω καὶ ἐνταῦθα μαχαίρας ἀκούοντες, μὴ τοῦτο νομίσωμεν, ὅτι ἐπέταξε μαχαίρας κεκτῆσθαι, ἀλλ' ὅτι διὰ τῶν μαχαιρῶν τὴν ἐνεστῶσαν αἰνίττεται ἐπιβουλὴν, καὶ ὅτι μέλλει πάσχειν παρὰ τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἅπερ ἔπαθε. Καὶ τοῦτο ἐκ τῶν ἑξῆς δῆλον. Εἰπὼν γὰρ, Ἀγοράσει μάχαιραν, ἐπήγαγε· Δεῖ γὰρ τὰ γεγραμμένα περὶ ἐμοῦ τελεσθῆναι, ὅτι ἐν τοῖς ἀνόμοις ἐλογίσθην. Εἰπόντων δὲ ἐκείνων, ὅτι Εἰσὶν ὧδε δύο μάχαιραι, καὶ τὸ λεχθὲν μὴ συνιέντων, φησὶν, Ἱκανόν ἐστι Καίτοι γε οὐκ ἦν ἱκανόν· εἰ μὲν γὰρ ἀνθρωπίνῃ βοηθείᾳ κεχρῆσθαι αὐτοὺς ἐβούλετο, οὐ μόνον δύο καὶ τρεῖς, ἀλλ' οὐδὲ ἑκατὸν ἦσαν ἱκαναὶ μάχαιραι· εἰ δὲ οὐκ ἐβούλετο ἀνθρωπίνῃ βοηθείᾳ αὐτοὺς κεχρῆσθαι, καὶ αἱ δύο περιτταί. Ἀλλ' ὅμως οὐκ ἐξεκάλυψε τὸ αἴνιγμα· καὶ γὰρ πολλαχοῦ φαίνεται τοῦτο ποιῶν· ἐπειδὰν μὴ νοήσωσι τὸ λεχθὲν, παρατρέχει καὶ ἀφίησι, τῇ τῶν πραγμάτων ἐκβάσει τῶν μετὰ ταῦτα τὴν κατανόησιν τῶν εἰρημένων ἐπιτρέπων λοιπόν· ὅπερ οὖν καὶ ἀλλαχοῦ ἐποίησε. Καὶ γὰρ περὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως αὐτοῦ διαλεγόμενος, οὕτω πως ἔλεγε· Λύσατε τὸν ναὸν τοῦτον, καὶ ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις ἐγερῶ αὐτόν. Καὶ ὅμως οὐκ ᾔδεισαν οἱ μαθηταὶ τὸ λεγόμενον· καὶ ὅτι οὐκ ᾔδεισαν, ὁ εὐαγγελιστὴς ἐπεσημήνατο, λέγων· Ὅτε δὲ ἀνέστη ὁ Ἰησοῦς, τότε ἐπίστευσαν τῷ λόγῳ αὐτοῦ, καὶ τῇ Γραφῆ. Καὶ πάλιν ἀλλαχοῦ· Οὐδὲ γὰρ ᾔδεισαν, ὅτι δεῖ αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῆναι. δʹ. Ἀλλὰ τὸ μὲν ζήτημα ἱκανὴν ἔχει τὴν λύσιν· ἡμεῖς δὲ ἐπὶ τὸ λειπόμενον τῆς προσρήσεως μέρος τὸν λόγον ἀγάγωμεν. Τί ποτ' οὖν ἐστι τὸ λεγόμενον, καὶ πόθεν εἰς ταῦτα ἐξέβημεν; Ἐμακαρίζομεν τὴν Πρίσκιλλαν καὶ τὸν Ἀκύλαν, ὅτι συνῴκουν τῷ Παύλῳ, ὅτι καὶ τὸν τρόπον τῆς στολῆς, καὶ τὸν τρόπον τῶν ὑποδημάτων, καὶ τὰ ἄλλα ἅπαντα μετὰ ἀκριβείας αὐτοῦ κατεμάνθανον. Ἐντεῦθεν τὸ ζήτημα ἡμῖν ἐτέχθη τοῦτο. Ἐζητοῦμεν γὰρ, τίνος ἕνεκεν, τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἀπαγορεύοντος μηδὲν ὅλως ἔχειν, εἰ μὴ μόνον ἱμάτιον, ἐφαίνοντο καὶ ὑποδήματα καὶ φελόνην ἔχοντες. Εἶτα ὁ λόγος ἀπέδειξεν, ὅτι οὐ παραβαίνοντες τὸν νόμον, ἀλλὰ καὶ σφόδρα τηροῦντες τούτοις ἐχρῶντο. Ταῦτα δὲ ἐλέγομεν, οὐκ εἰς περιουσίαν χρημάτων ὑμᾶς ἀλείφοντες, οὐδὲ παρακαλοῦντες πλείω τῆς χρείας κεκτῆσθαι, ἀλλ' ἵνα ἔχητε πρὸς τοὺς ἀπίστους ἀντιλέγειν τοὺς διαχλευάζοντας τὰ ἡμέτερα.
thought_title: The sword saying as a riddle for the coming plot
orientation: Chrysostom is explaining why Christ told the disciples to buy a sword, arguing that the command was a riddle pointing to the plot against him, not a literal instruction to arm themselves.
pass_a_gloss: And this he did not wish to say openly, but through riddles, so as not to disturb them again. Just as therefore when you hear him saying, that 'What you heard into the ear, proclaim upon the housetops, and what you heard in the darkness, say in the light,' you do not suspect this, that he commands them to leave the narrow streets and the marketplace and proclaim upon the housetops; for the disciples do not appear to have done this; but the 'Upon the housetops,' and the 'In the light,' hints at the boldness; and the 'Into the ear,' and the 'In the darkness,' makes this clear, that 'What you heard in a small part of the inhabited world, and in one region of Palestine, this you are to sound out everywhere on the earth.' For he was not indeed speaking to them in darkness, nor into the ear, but on high mountains, and in the synagogues often. So also here one must understand it. Just as therefore there, hearing housetops, we understood it differently, so also here, hearing swords, let us not think this, that he commanded them to possess swords, but that through the swords he hints at the present plot, and that he is about to suffer from the Jews, the very things which he suffered. And this is clear from what follows. For having said, 'He will buy a sword,' he added: 'For it is necessary that the things written about me be fulfilled, that he was reckoned among the lawless.' And when those said, that 'There are two swords here,' and did not understand what was said, he says, 'It is enough.' And yet it was not enough; for if he wanted them to use human help, not only two and three, but not even a hundred swords were enough; but if he did not want them to use human help, even the two were superfluous. But nevertheless he did not uncover the riddle; for he appears doing this in many places; whenever they do not understand what was said, he passes by and lets it go, entrusting the understanding of what was said to the outcome of events after these things; which indeed he also did elsewhere. For also when discussing his resurrection, he spoke in this way: 'Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it.' And yet the disciples did not know what was said; and that they did not know, the evangelist noted, saying: 'But when Jesus rose, then they believed his word, and the Scripture.' And again elsewhere: 'For they did not know that it was necessary for him to rise from the dead.' 4. But the question has a sufficient solution; let us bring the discourse to the remaining part of the greeting. What then is the saying, and from where did we digress to these things? We were calling Priscilla and Aquila blessed, because they lived with Paul, because they learned accurately from him the manner of his clothing, and the manner of his sandals, and all the other things. From there this question was born for us. For we were asking, for what reason, when Christ forbade having anything at all, except only a cloak, they appeared having both sandals and a cloak. Then the discourse showed, that not transgressing the law, but rather keeping it very much, they used these things. And we were saying these things, not anointing you toward abundance of money, nor urging you to possess more than need, but so that you may have something to say against the unbelievers who mock our things.

choices.why: Chrysostom uses this term repeatedly for Christ's indirect sayings; 'riddles' preserves the sense of hidden meaning requiring interpretation.
The literal rendering keeps the spatial image that Chrysostom then reinterprets as boldness.
The verb conveys indirect signification, which is the core of Chrysostom's argument about the sword saying.
The term refers to the hostile scheme against Christ; 'plot' captures the conspiratorial sense.
The verb means to reveal or disclose; 'uncovered' preserves the image of the riddle remaining veiled.
The term refers to the result or issue of events; 'outcome' fits the sense of later events clarifying earlier sayings.

pass_b_english: And this he did not want to say openly, but through riddles, so as not to disturb them again. So when you hear him say, “What you have heard in the ear, proclaim upon the housetops, and what you have heard in the dark, speak in the light” (Matthew 10:27), you do not suspect that he is commanding them to leave the narrow streets and the marketplace and preach on the housetops—for the disciples do not appear to have done this. Rather, “upon the housetops” and “in the light” hint at boldness, while “in the ear” and “in the dark” mean this: what you heard in one small part of the world, in one region of Palestine, sound it out everywhere on earth. For he did not speak to them in the dark or in the ear, but on high mountains and often in the synagogues.

So we must understand it the same way here. Just as there, when we hear “housetops,” we understood it differently, so here, when we hear “swords,” let us not think that he commanded them to possess swords, but that through the swords he hints at the present plot, and that he was about to suffer from the Jews what he did suffer. And this is clear from what follows. For after saying, “Buy a sword,” he added, “For what is written about me must be fulfilled: ‘I was reckoned among the lawless’” (Luke 22:36-37). And when they said, “Here are two swords,” not understanding what was said, he says, “It is enough” (Luke 22:38). Yet it was not enough. For if he wanted them to use human help, not only two or three, but not even a hundred swords would have been enough. But if he did not want them to use human help, then even the two were superfluous.

Still, he did not uncover the riddle. For he appears to do this in many places: when they do not understand what is said, he passes by and leaves it, entrusting the understanding of what was said to the outcome of events afterward. This is what he did elsewhere as well. For when speaking about his resurrection, he said something like this: “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up” (John 2:19). And yet the disciples did not know what was said. And that they did not know, the evangelist noted, saying, “When Jesus rose, then they believed his word and the Scripture” (John 2:22). And again elsewhere: “For they did not yet know that he must rise from the dead” (John 20:9).

But the question has a sufficient answer. Let us bring our discussion to the remaining part of the greeting. What then is being said, and how did we get onto these things? We were blessing Priscilla and Aquila, because they lived with Paul, because they learned from him with precision even the manner of his clothing, the manner of his sandals, and everything else. From this our question was born. For we were asking why, when Christ forbade having anything at all except only a garment, they appeared to have sandals and a cloak. Then the argument showed that they were not breaking the law, but were keeping it very strictly in using these things. And we were saying these things not to train you toward an abundance of possessions, nor to urge you to acquire more than you need, but so that you may have an answer for unbelievers who mock our ways.
